newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares end lower after profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: French shares end lower after profit-taking.

text.p: French shares ended lower after a gust of profit-taking took the Paris bourse lower in late afternoon trading.
Traders said a slip in the dollar against the mark, later corrected, sent a signal for investors to book profits on some of the market's recent strong rise.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 23.06 points or 0.85 percent at 2,686.15.
The CAC-40 futures contract was down 19 points at 2,696 from Monday's close.
Lafarge fell 3.14 percent to 367.5 francs, weighed by profit-taking ahead of 1996 results due on Wednesday.
Analysts expect the building materials company will report profit lower than 1995, with net attributable gain of 1.9-2.0 billion francs against 2.35 billion in 1995.
Embattled car firm Renault dropped 4.25 percent to 133 francs, with brokers citing the continuing row over a Belgian plant closure.
Banque Nationale de Paris fell 2.35 percent, hit by a newspaper report insurer Axa-UAP planned to cut its holding in the bank.
The stock rose strongly last week on the back of strong profits.
Oil firm Total bucked the trend, rising 0.43 percent, helped by a report Axa-UAP would also sell half of its Elf-Aquitaine stake to buy Total stock. Elf was down 0.69 percent at 578.
Canal Plus was also among the rare risers, up 2.27 percent at 1,125. The broadcaster has been supported by hopes of a launch of a single Spanish digital television service.
Among the biggest falls were Cie Generale des Eaux, Eridania Beghin-Say, Legrand, Danone and Promodes -- all down by more than two percent.
Soon-to-be-privatised Thomson-CSF fell 1.62 percent to 194.1 francs.
The government said after the close that offers for the sell-off should be in by March 28 and it would pick the winner by June 30.

It earlier named Marcel Roulet as chairman of Thomson-CSF, to work on its privatisation, and put in an ex-Cie des Machines Bull executive, Thierry Breton, to head Thomson SA and to prepare the Multimedia subsidiary for privatisation.
